stem: A business impact analysis lists a claims-processing application as recoverable within eight hours because its own servers can be restored quickly. During an outage, the team discovers that the process also depends on a third-party identity service and a specialized data feed whose contracts provide no comparable recovery commitment. What is the BEST BIA correction?
decision_point: analyze end-to-end business-process dependencies and validate supplier recovery assumptions before setting achievable recovery requirements
misconceptions: application server recovery time alone defines business-process RTO
third-party dependencies belong only to procurement
a contractual relationship guarantees aligned recovery capability

originality.authoring_note: Original BIA scenario focused on hidden third-party dependencies and whether stated recovery objectives are achievable end to end.

options: Keep the eight-hour estimate because only internally operated systems belong in the BIA

Map the complete business process and its critical internal/external dependencies, assess the impact and maximum tolerable disruption, validate dependency recovery capabilities and contractual assumptions, then set or revise recovery requirements and strategies accordingly
Remove third-party services from continuity planning because the organization cannot directly control them
Set every dependency to the same RTO as the application without checking whether suppliers can meet it
explanation: A BIA should reflect the business process and the dependencies required to deliver it. Recovery objectives are credible only when critical suppliers, data feeds, identity services, people, facilities, and other dependencies are understood and addressed.
distractor_rationales: Recovering an application does not restore the business process if required external services remain unavailable.

A BIA should reflect the business process and the dependencies required to deliver it. Recovery objectives are credible only when critical suppliers, data feeds, identity services, people, facilities, and other dependencies are understood and addressed.
Lack of direct control increases the need to understand and manage external-dependency risk rather than excluding it.
An unvalidated target assigned to a supplier is not evidence that the dependency can meet the business requirement.

stem: A data-exchange platform labels records by integrity level. High-integrity accounting data may be read by lower-integrity reporting processes, but management wants to prevent those lower-integrity processes from modifying the accounting records. Which formal security-model principle BEST matches this requirement?
decision_point: apply Biba-style integrity reasoning so lower-integrity subjects cannot write to higher-integrity objects
misconceptions: Bell-LaPadula is primarily an integrity model
confidentiality labels alone prevent low-integrity modification
read and write rules are identical across confidentiality and integrity models

originality.authoring_note: Original formal-model application scenario requiring Biba integrity reasoning rather than memorization of model names alone.

options: Use Bell-LaPadula's confidentiality focus because it primarily prevents lower-integrity subjects from modifying higher-integrity data
Apply Biba-style integrity controls that prevent lower-integrity subjects from writing to higher-integrity objects while designing read rules according to the system's integrity policy
Remove integrity labels and rely only on encryption at rest
Allow lower-integrity writers as long as they can read the high-integrity records first
explanation: Biba is an integrity-oriented model. A central goal is preventing less trustworthy subjects or data from contaminating higher-integrity objects, commonly summarized with a no-write-up integrity rule in the simple model formulation.
distractor_rationales: Bell-LaPadula is principally concerned with confidentiality and information disclosure, not preventing lower-integrity writes into higher-integrity objects.

Biba is an integrity-oriented model. A central goal is preventing less trustworthy subjects or data from contaminating higher-integrity objects, commonly summarized with a no-write-up integrity rule in the simple model formulation.
Encryption protects confidentiality of stored data but does not enforce integrity-level write relationships between subjects and objects.
Permission to read does not imply permission to modify a higher-integrity object.

stem: A serverless application uses dozens of short-lived functions. Each function receives the same broad cloud role, can access every data store in the account, and implicitly trusts any event arriving from the internal event bus. Which architecture improvement BEST addresses the security characteristics of this computing model?
decision_point: treat each function/event path as an independent workload trust boundary with scoped identity, explicit event validation, least privilege, secret management, and observable lifecycle controls
misconceptions: short-lived functions need less access governance
internal event buses are inherently trusted
one shared cloud role simplifies security without increasing blast radius

originality.authoring_note: Sibling of the released serverless least-privilege scenario family, but emphasizes event-source trust boundaries and per-function workload identity across a distributed serverless architecture.

options: Keep the broad shared role because short-lived functions cannot retain access long enough to create material risk

Assign narrowly scoped workload identities to functions, validate and authorize event sources/claims, minimize data-store permissions, manage secrets outside code, and preserve logging/monitoring across ephemeral executions
Move all functions into one larger function so there is only one identity to govern
Trust every event on the internal bus automatically because internal messaging is outside the attack surface
explanation: Serverless reduces server-management burden but not identity, authorization, input-trust, secret, or observability requirements. Per-workload identities and explicit event/data trust controls limit blast radius in highly distributed ephemeral systems.
distractor_rationales: Short execution duration does not prevent a compromised function from abusing broad privileges immediately.

Serverless reduces server-management burden but not identity, authorization, input-trust, secret, or observability requirements. Per-workload identities and explicit event/data trust controls limit blast radius in highly distributed ephemeral systems.
Combining functions can increase privilege aggregation and coupling rather than solving authorization design.
Internal event infrastructure can carry spoofed, compromised, or unauthorized events and should not automatically erase trust boundaries.

stem: A threat model for an AI-assisted customer-support system covers prompt injection and data leakage from the language model, but it treats all actions taken by the model's tools as trusted once the model decides to call them. The agent can issue refunds, change customer contact information, and open internal tickets through separate APIs. What is the BEST threat-modeling improvement?
decision_point: model tool invocation, authorization boundaries, confused-deputy and indirect-instruction abuse paths, high-impact action constraints, and human/transaction controls rather than treating agent tool calls as inherently trusted
misconceptions: model output can be trusted as authorization
prompt filtering alone controls downstream tool abuse
internal APIs need no separate threat boundaries when invoked by an agent

originality.authoring_note: Sibling of the released iterative AI-agent threat-model update, but focuses specifically on modeling tool authority, confused-deputy behavior, and downstream high-impact action abuse.

options: Keep the model unchanged because the language model already decides whether a tool call is appropriate

Extend the threat model across each tool/API trust boundary: analyze indirect instructions, confused-deputy and privilege abuse, per-action authorization, transaction limits, user intent binding, sensitive-action confirmation or human review where appropriate, logging, rollback, and abuse cases for downstream effects
Remove logging from tool calls because logs could contain sensitive prompts
Grant the agent one administrator API token so all tool authorization decisions are centralized in the model
explanation: Agentic systems expand the attack surface beyond model text. Threat modeling should include the authority of downstream tools, how user or external content can influence actions, and controls that independently constrain and authorize high-impact operations.
distractor_rationales: A model's decision is not equivalent to an independent authorization decision and can be influenced by malicious or ambiguous inputs.

Agentic systems expand the attack surface beyond model text. Threat modeling should include the authority of downstream tools, how user or external content can influence actions, and controls that independently constrain and authorize high-impact operations.
Sensitive logging requires careful design, but removing action visibility weakens detection and accountability.
A broad administrator token increases blast radius and makes model manipulation more consequential.
